facts.text: Bel Air earned its name when court records dropped two letters in 1798, turning “Belle Aire” into the town’s current spelling.
The town became Harford County’s seat just two years after its founding, with Daniel Scott building a courthouse on Main Street in 1782.
The Maryland and Pennsylvania Railroad once ran through Bel Air, but its tracks were dismantled in 1958 and later turned into the Ma and Pa walking trail.
The historic Hays House Museum, a preserved 18th‑century home, offers a glimpse into Bel Air’s early days and is a key local landmark.
Bel Air’s castle‑like Armory, built in the early 20th century, stands as a prominent reminder of the town’s military and community heritage.
Originally part of a 1731 land grant to Daniel Scott, the area that is now Bel Air was first called “Scott’s Old Fields.”.
